title: The Mystery School's complete library
acceptance: Every one of the 66 School records is readable in RISE: 60 in English from a named, hashed, proofed public-domain edition; the rest in their original language with the language named; the Gate's Latin served and its RISE translation after the owner has read it.

The School's texts live in a School corpus with its own manifest, build loop and checksum gate; CANON, LIBRARY_TEXTS, the Library's cards and counts, certification and the decision catalogue are unchanged and the Archive's Standard-Ebooks-only rule stays true for the Archive.

Every served School text passes the ingest gates: words reconciled against the source artifact, no distributor matter, declared unit names, verse lineation kept; the Lectern shows the edition actually used and the life+70 status.
The owner's four questions in the investigation record are answered and recorded before PR 1 merges.

evidence.note: Investigation (every link opened 2026-10-16), the School corpus design, the six-PR build order and the owner's questions.
PR 1: the School corpus mechanism, the Standard Ebooks adapter and ten texts; the School goes from 4 to 14 readable.
PR 1 merged (#710): the corpus mechanism and ten Standard Ebooks texts.

PR 2 merged (#712) and deployed: the Gutenberg adapter and 24 texts; 38 readable.
PR 3: Wikisource, CCEL, sacred-texts, TEI, Victorian Web and file adapters; 20 texts and the Gate's Latin; 58 readable.

summary: After RDR-029 shipped with four of 66 texts readable, the owner lifted the Standard-Ebooks-only serving rule for the School only. The survey finds a free proofed edition for 46 of the 62 missing texts, nine as scans needing a proofing pass, and six with no free English, the Gate among them. The design admits them through a School corpus beside the Archive, on the Chapel's precedent, with recipes per work and the same gates every time; six pull requests take the School from 4 to 66 readable.
